handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

key_findings_and_decisions: road_LF = sum of each street alignment's stationing span (end_sta - start_sta), HAND-ENTERED from plan sheets. DWG geometry over-counts (offset/construction lines, profile copies, cul-de-sac/intersection centerlines) and which layer is least-bad flips per job; station text isn't in these DWGs. So DWG is cross-check only.
Entity-count tell: Woodman's clean centerline was a single LWPOLYLINE (n=1). Contaminated layers have many entities (Lone Fir C-ROAD-CNTR n=11). Use as a smell test, not a rule.
The qty sheet + proposal are the COMPLETE spine for as-bid quantities/prices. Geometry-only DWGs do not create quantity holes. DWG stays tertiary (confirms the Phase 0->1 pivot).

Two firms use a non-NCS layer scheme (SV-/SF-/SS-/CNTL) — Settlement Mountain and Painted Rock. They have NO clean road centerline layer (Settlement SV-CNTL-PROP-LIN=11851 is inflated, ~= property-line length; not road centerline). road_LF for these MUST be hand-read. Did NOT add 'CNTL' to the matcher (ambiguous control-vs-centerline, would inject bad numbers).

Lone Fir & Mountainside are single-main-road jobs (road + lots; Mountainside has minor parking slits), so the single station span = full road_LF. Other jobs' single-vs-multi-street status is unconfirmed — multi-street jobs need EACH street's span summed.

Mountainside DWG path: only two DWGs exist (CBASE_SENT CAD.dwg + XREF/VBASE2.dwg); BOTH are processed by the manifest entry. No third file. The survey xref's V-ROAD-CNTR (800) was closer to the 680 stationing truth than the civil C-ROAD-CNTR (1180) — reinforces 'DWG unreliable for road_LF'.
The road_LF_dwg_mismatch flags that will appear on Lone Fir (~246%) and Mountainside (~74%) are EXPECTED and CORRECT — they prove the geometry was wrong and the stationing is right.
